content.value_statement: Lark CLI setup and permission failures can be difficult to diagnose. This skill provides structured authentication, identity, approval, and token-routing workflows.
actual_capabilities: Initializes Lark CLI application configuration and presents authorization links with QR codes.
Checks user and bot identity, login status, token validity, and granted scopes.
Starts scoped user authorization through domain, scope, and split device-code flows.
Explains bot and user permission errors using returned scope and console details.
Handles structured success, error, update notice, and confirmation-required responses.
Routes Wiki node tokens to the correct underlying Lark resource skill.
limitations: Requires lark-cli to be installed and an application configuration to be available.
Cannot grant bot scopes; an administrator must enable them in the Lark developer console.
User authorization requires an interactive browser or QR-code confirmation.
Cannot revoke one server-side scope through the CLI; users may need the authorization management page.

use_cases.title: Set Up Developer Authentication
use_cases.description: Initialize Lark CLI, complete scoped user authorization, and verify the resulting identity and token.

use_cases.title: Resolve Workspace Permission Errors
use_cases.description: Distinguish user and bot scope failures, then identify the correct console or authorization action.

use_cases.title: Build Safer Lark Automations
use_cases.description: Interpret structured responses, preview risky operations, and preserve confirmation gates before writes.

prompt_templates.title: Check Login Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my current Lark CLI login status and active identity. Verify the token, then summarize granted scopes without exposing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Lark CLI
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize a new Lark CLI application configuration. Start the process in the background, then show the unchanged authorization URL and QR code.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Missing Permissions
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this Lark CLI permission error: [paste error]. Identify the active identity and recommend the minimum required scope or administrator action.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Risky Operation
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview this Lark operation with dry-run: [operation]. Explain its risk and parameters, then wait for explicit approval before any confirmed retry.

output_examples.input: Check my Lark CLI login and token status.
output_examples.output: Active identity: user. Token verification succeeded. The session has calendar read access. No secret values were displayed.

output_examples.input: Why can my bot not read a user's drive files?
output_examples.output: The bot identity cannot access personal user resources. Enable the required bot scope, or use an authorized user identity when the operation requires user access.

output_examples.input: Delete this drive item after checking the request.
output_examples.output: The preview identifies a high-risk deletion and shows the target item. Explicit approval is required before the operation can be retried.

best_practices: Request the smallest domain or scope that satisfies the task.
Verify the active user or bot identity before diagnosing access failures.
Use dry-run and obtain explicit approval before retrying high-risk writes.
anti_patterns: Do not expose application secrets, access tokens, device codes, or cached authorization links.
Do not run user authorization for bot identities or assume bots can access personal resources.
Do not append confirmation flags before the user explicitly approves the displayed high-risk action.

faq.question: Does this skill store credentials?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the agent to avoid exposing secrets and does not include credential storage code.

faq.question: Can it authorize a bot with the login command?
faq.answer: No. Bot scopes must be enabled in the developer console; interactive login applies to user identities.

faq.question: Can I request only one permission?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a specific scope when possible, or select a limited business domain.

faq.question: Can it revoke one granted scope?
faq.answer: No. The CLI cannot revoke one server-side scope; use minimal reauthorization or the authorization management page.

faq.question: How are dangerous write operations handled?
faq.answer: The workflow previews requests when needed and requires explicit user approval before adding the confirmation flag.

faq.question: Does it support Wiki links?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to inspect Wiki node links and route the underlying object token to the correct Lark skill.
